title: Evaluate the 4,265-term Clifford identity row on a compact input with one Gauss sum
body:
The identity row in #7800 requires exactly 151 × 2⁴⁷ coordinate probes on arbitrary dense data. When its input is instead the absolute-phase affine-quadratic chart emitted by Ali Romman's circuit simulator, the 22 address groups share a translation space. One quadratic Gauss sum on at most 52 binary variables supplies the anchor for all 4,265 weighted Fourier terms. The implementation still performs linear solves, phase transport and signed accumulation.

An explicit circuit prepares an observation supported on all 2¹⁰⁴ addresses and outside the Clifford-column span. Its exact output is 2⁻²⁹, checked by separate Fourier factorization. On the stated 104-bit phase-mask tape, one active cell uses 104 reads, 208 input-head moves including restoration, and 401 bytes of fixed lookup data. That tape price is for one cell and the declared encoding.

The registered verification includes all 4,233 Fourier values through dimension three, 22 bounded-support circuit fixtures, four normalized Clifford columns, 137 tape masks, and the public JSON example. Credit goes to Ali Romman for #5704 and #5727, and to the Bell-fibre and signed-row work in #7799 and #7800. Connecting the chart to a multiplication supplier remains open.

Canonical base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. All four registered commands passed under CPython 3.12.14, both locally and from the read-only, Git-free export of the published commit. The package passed the repository’s committed-byte, file-mode, source-history and export checks.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-chart-contraction
```

Prepared by apoursh with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Maintainer scientific review is open. The selected conditional multiplication exponent is unchanged.
